mac.environment: one local macOS 26.3.1 arm64, task-owned FD3 fixture
mac.oldSource: front succeeded; enqueue trapped before intent creation because string-to-string FS2 B was unsupported
mac.byteWriteWithOldDeletion: queue updated and intent remained, but process trapped at unsupported FS2 J; following front refused pending-unknown
mac.final: byte B plus FS2 L to archive intent; sequential cases, race, and independently held lock passed

linux.environment: isolated ARM64 VM, 1 CPU, 2 GiB; removed after test
linux.contract: 7 sequential checks, 2 synthetic pending/intent, malformed state, 8 concurrent attempts; 1 enqueued and 7 busy
linux.processKill: instrumented enqueue SIGKILL after intent, pending, queue rename or directory sync: uninstrumented front refuses pending-unknown; after intent archive: uninstrumented front returns the committed ticket

limits: Mac uses diagnostic compiler/packager, not a release runtime. Single host and one concurrent sample. Linux SIGKILL uses deliberately instrumented fixture; no power loss, fsync failure, Mac SIGKILL, attacker path races, FIFO admission fairness, workload/process-tree lifecycle, resource limits, full governor or fleet qualification. Python is used only for fixture observation and staging.
